report:
## Verdict: REJECT (checklist FAIL on criterion 5; owner-mismatch ERROR log omits the store class)
The PR is not ready to merge: when `truncate_messages` raises `ConversationOwnerMismatchError`, the trim's ERROR log names only the conversation, not the store class that criterion 5 requires.
Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings
### 🔴 Critical
- VC-21: FAIL (critical) — When a trim is needed and the conversation store has no `truncate_messages`, or reading the conversation or calling `truncate_messages` raises, the call logs at ERROR naming the store class, leaves the history as it was, and returns or raises the same result it would have without the trim. [src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:309] — fix the code, or have the issue author amend this criterion

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Criterion 5 counts (criteria.json is a valid list with criterion 5 matching this claim). In _trim_unanswered_tool_use (src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:266-356), alternatives split: (a) get_conversation raises (285-294) -> ERROR via logger.exception naming type(store).__name__, returns: conforms. (b) no truncate_messages (309-319) -> logger.error naming the store class, returns: conforms. (c) truncate_messages raises generic Exception (331-340) -> logger.exception naming the store class: conforms. (d) truncate_messages raises ConversationOwnerMismatchError (322-330) -> logger.error WITHOUT type(store).__name__ (message only has the conversation id): departure from 'logs at ERROR naming the store class'. This is a store fault inside the trigger (truncate_messages raising) and no sibling criterion names it. (e) scanning stored messages raises (297-305) -> ERROR without store class either; arguably outside the literal 'reading the conversation' wording but also a silent-departure fault. History is left unchanged and the function returns without raising in all branches, so the 'same result' part holds; only the store-class naming fails for (d) (and (e)). The comment at 322-330 does not justify the omission.

  </details>

### 🟠 Important / Major
1. `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 322-330: the `except ConversationOwnerMismatchError` arm of `_trim_unanswered_tool_use` logs ERROR with only the conversation id. Criterion 5 requires an ERROR log naming the store class when calling `truncate_messages` raises. The scan-failure arm (lines 299-305) also omits the store class. Checklist item VC-21 confirms this. (raised by 2/4 agents) [unmet-decided-criterion carve-out] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=not-held limb-one=not-evaluated limb-two=not-evaluated; evidence: log content is program output that criterion 5 requires -->
2. `tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py` line 4: the module docstring says a stopped `query_database` call never leaves an unanswered `tool_use`. The trim's failure arms (no `truncate_messages`, truncate raises or removes nothing, read raises) leave it in place, and the file's own parametrized test asserts that. Checklist item VC-15 confirms this. (raised by 1/4 agents) [self-contradicting-diff carve-out] <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=not-held limb-one=not-evaluated limb-two=not-evaluated; evidence: the docstring makes a claim about what the trim mechanism covers, so it counts as a functional-coverage claim -->

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (3)
<details><summary>3 items</summary>

1. `tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py` lines 600-608: the parametrized failure-path test has no case for the owner-mismatch arm or the scan-failure arm, so their logging is untested. (raised by 1/4 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 342-347: the "removed nothing" ERROR message says the next call "may be rejected", while its three sibling messages say "will be rejected". The outcome is the same in all four cases. (raised by 1/4 agents)
- VC-15: FAIL (suggestion) — Module docstring: a stopped query_database call never leaves an unanswered tool_use. [tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py:4]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The module docstring (tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py:4) states without qualification that a stopped query_database call never leaves an unanswered tool_use. src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py:266-345 _trim_unanswered_tool_use has failure branches that deliberately leave it in place and only log ERROR. A store without truncate_messages hits the early return at 310-319 (log text: 'left an unanswered tool_use that was not removed ... has no truncate_messages'). ConversationOwnerMismatchError (322-330) and any other Exception from truncate (331+) are logged and the function returns, as do get_conversation raising (286-294) and a scan error (299-305). The function's own docstring says the cleanup 'Never raises' and logs rather than removes. The file's own parametrized test, per the verify_hint, asserts the tool_use stays in those cases. The default BoundedConversationStore has truncate_messages, so the default path is covered, but embedder-supplied stores are a documented input (the code comments at 596-604 name embedder-supplied conversation_store). The claim therefore overstates the guarantee: it holds only for stores that implement truncate_messages and do not raise. The rejection about a None return from truncate_messages concerns a different defect (the falsy-return check) and does not cover this item. Impact is a wording overstatement in a test docstring.

  </details>

</details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With the real `Agent` and a `BoundedConversationStore`, a `query_database_impl_with_widgets` call on conversation C that is cancelled after the agent saved an assistant `tool_use` and before it saved the matching `tool_result` leaves C with exactly the messages it had before that call, and the next call on C sends an Anthropic request in which every `tool_use` block is directly followed by a `tool_result` block with the same id, and returns a non-error result.
- [ ] With the real `Agent` and a `BoundedConversationStore`, a `query_database_impl_with_widgets` call on conversation C that ends without cancellation while a `tool_use` it saved has no `tool_result` leaves C cut back to just before the earliest assistant message that call saved with an unanswered `tool_use` — every message before it stays, the call's user message included — logs a WARNING naming C and the number of messages removed, and the next call on C sends an Anthropic request in which every `tool_use` block is directly followed by a `tool_result` block with the same id, and returns a non-error result. A `tool_use` counts as unanswered when its id, taken from the assistant message's `tool_calls` or from a `tool_use` block in its `provider_content`, has no `role="tool"` message directly after that assistant message.
- [ ] A call that ends without cancellation and saved an unanswered `tool_use` still returns the error it returns today: an `AgentRunError` with the `SQL execution error: ` prefix when the agent returned an error answer, and the same `RuntimeError`, with the same message, that it raises today when `send_message` raised.
- [ ] A call that ends without cancellation and saved no unanswered `tool_use` leaves C's history exactly as the call appended it: a failed call's user message stays ahead of the next call's, as `tests/unit/test_query_database_queue.py` pins.
- [ ] When a trim is needed and the conversation store has no `truncate_messages`, or reading the conversation or calling `truncate_messages` raises, the call logs at ERROR naming the store class, leaves the history as it was, and returns or raises the same result it would have without the trim.
- [ ] The change leaves the vendored Anthropic request builder (`_build_payload` in `src/sqllens/agent/integrations/anthropic/llm.py`) unchanged, so a conversation that reaches it with an unmatched `tool_use` by a path other than `query_database` is still sent as it is.
